_about: Historical rollout policy retained for diagnostic compatibility until #1593. Issue #1592 supersedes mandatory epic targeting: the dates below are historical, auto mode is permanently advisory, and new work follows docs/source/development/github-flow.rst. No live setting is changed by this file.

rollout.note: Cancelled by #1592 before activation. Both this 2026-12-15 schedule and epic_branch.py's 2026-12-21 schedule are historical; automatic mode remains advisory regardless of dates or environment overrides. Explicit strict is retained only for historical diagnostics pending #1593.
rollout.ci_coverage_note: The four workflows whose pull_request trigger carries epic/** since this rollout, so a child PR into epic/<slug> runs the same required checks as one into develop. This is an addition of coverage and no path in any of them may skip a check for a branch, an author or a label.

branch_lifecycle.created_by: a person, from the repository's branch settings, from the tip of origin/develop
branch_lifecycle.created_when: when the epic's first child is approved and claimed
branch_lifecycle.deleted_by: the person who merged the epic's integration PR, in the same act
branch_lifecycle.never_by_an_agent: creation, deletion, rename, force-push, retarget and protection are human-only acts
branch_lifecycle.merge_queue: child PRs are not queued (the epic branch is the integration point and a plain human-approved merge commit merges them); the epic's integration PR into develop uses the queue like any other PR into develop

bootstrap.reason: Rule 16 of the contract: enforcing an epic branch on the epic that has to build the enforcement is a cycle, so this epic's own children follow R3 and target develop. The exemption ends when the epic's integration PR merges, and the tool verifies that instead of trusting a date: an epic listed here whose epic/<slug> branch stands with no integration PR open is reported as an unfinished bootstrap.

legacy_exceptions.reason: In-flight epic named by the contract's Migration of existing work: four of its seven children are already merged into develop, so cutting a branch now would give the remaining children an integration target their siblings never had, and retargeting the open child PRs is the disruption the epic objective forbids. It adopts the contract at its next un-started child, which is also when it owes the `slug:` declaration rule 1 requires (it has none, so R3 covers it until then).

legacy_exceptions_note: Every entry is an epic a person recorded, with the issue that records it and an expiry date. An entry past its `expires` date stops exempting anything: the plan reports `legacy-exception-expired` and the epic is judged on the contract's own rows, so an exception cannot quietly become permanent. A bootstrap exemption belongs in `bootstrap`, not here - the two are different facts and are checked differently.
